pdf_file_read: 1998 SHRINK - Kubat, Holte, Matwin.pdf (Drive id 1W9DubnXJROPbPHHYcvOI1SXvE7I3OC6g; Kubat, Holte, Matwin, 'Machine Learning for the Detection of Oil Spills in Satellite Radar Images', Machine Learning 30, 195-215, 1998; 21 PDF pages)

datasets.name: oil spill (regions from 9 RADARSAT/ERS-1 satellite radar images)
datasets.class_distribution: 41 positives / 896 negatives (per image positives 8 4 2 6 2 4 3 5 7; negatives 3 180 101 129 60 70 76 80 197; totals 11 184 103 135 62 74 79 85 204)
datasets.ir_printed: the majority class thus comprises almost 96% of the data
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Dark regions extracted by Macdonald Dettwiler image-processing from 9 images (strait of Juan de Fuca), labelled by a human expert as oil slick vs lookalike; all lookalike subtypes kept as one nonspill class (p.6, p.11, p.12-13). For Figs 3-4, negatives were randomly sampled to varying numbers (p.13).
datasets.ref: Table 2, p.11 (printed p.205); 49 features p.12-13 (printed p.206-207); 41/896 p.5 (printed p.199)

ir_definition_ref: p.5 (printed p.199): imbalance described only as 'majority class thus comprises almost 96% of the data'

baselines_all: Solberg and Solberg (1996) decision tree (reported accuracies only, discussed in Sec. 8)

chosen.metric: g-mean (paper's main measure; no SMOTE comparison exists)

outcome.stat_test: t-test mentioned for C4.5 with one-sided selection improvement (p.14, printed p.208); none for SHRINK vs SMOTE

win_claim.quote: Our solutions to these issues are implemented in the Canadian Environmental Hazards Detection System (CEHDS), which is about to undergo field testing.

uncertain: Drive file titled SHRINK is the 1998 Machine Learning oil-spill paper; SHRINK itself was introduced in Kubat, Holte & Matwin (1997) ECML 'Learning when Negative Examples Abound', which reports other datasets (p.11, printed p.205)
source_repo set to 'private': paper says data from sponsor Macdonald Dettwiler, does not state public release (p.4, printed p.198)
n_features=49 taken from text 'a region is described by 49 features' (p.12, printed p.206); feature set changed during project (p.13)
notes: Paper predates SMOTE (2002); no SMOTE baseline. SHRINK results only as plots (Fig. 4, p.15/printed p.209: g-mean, acc+, acc- vs number of negatives, 5x10-fold CV; Fig. 5 ROC curve) and Table 4 (p.16, printed p.210) SHRINK theta=0: CV g-mean 70.9, acc+ 82.5, acc- 60.9; LOBO g-mean 62.5, acc+ 78.1, acc- 50.1. Table 3 (p.14, printed p.208) one-sided selection: C4.5 g-mean 81.1, acc+ 76.0, acc- 86.6; 1-NN 67.2, 54.0, 83.4. g-mean defined as sqrt(acc+ x acc-) (p.9, printed p.203). Evaluation: 5 random runs of 10-fold CV, and leave-one-batch-out (LOBO). Related method one-sided selection (Kubat & Matwin 1997).
